clue.text: Manx TT

parts.note: the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man is literally a contest held on an island; the phrase also names the British people

explanation.walkthrough: The Manx TT is the famous motorcycle road race on the Isle of Man. The answer is also a stock phrase for the British.
explanation.definitionFit: A race held on an island is literally that, and the stock phrase is also a nickname for the British nation.

clue.text: It's off, all right

definitions.meaning: said of a dish on a menu: none remaining, all gone
read literally: every turn is a right turn, so no lefts remain

explanation.definitionFit: A menu item that is off has been used up, and a set that is all rights contains no lefts at all.

clue.text: Kind of jacket, characteristic to a point

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass points
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: Describing a jacket's distinctive feature, one that tapers to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait-jacket is the restraining garment, so this word names a kind of jacket.

clue.text: Was sorry for sounding discourteous

indicators.note: the clue says the word for discourteous is heard, giving a spelling that sounds alike

parts.note: rude means discourteous

explanation.surface: Someone regretted coming across as impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, so the past tense means was sorry for.

clue.text: A thousand goose-step around the Bucks. village

indicators.note: around signals the letters being turned about and rearranged

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A thousand soldiers march with a goose-step around a Buckinghamshire village.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks. is Buckinghamshire, an English county; Stoke Poges is the village of Gray's Elegy churchyard. K and GOOSESTEP are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoke Poges is a real village in Buckinghamshire, famous for Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.

clue.text: "Open nothing up" — US leader

parts.note: frank means open, candid

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A slogan from an American politician urging people to reveal nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was a Founding Father and leading figure of the early United States.

clue.text: A name is called a name

indicators.note: called here means spoken out, so what follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a moniker is a name

explanation.surface: A circular remark that a name is just called a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Monica is a girl's first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Expression of surprise at the short tall story

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in amazement at a short, exaggerated tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a fictional or invented story, as is a tall story.

clue.text: Put on the green!

parts.note: the word put is a golf putt missing a letter, so it is a putt cut down in length

explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that 'Put' is literally 'putt' cut short; on the golf green a short putt is a tap-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief tap of the ball on the golf green is called by this golfing phrase.

clue.text: Spacious, though cold and damp to the ear

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rheumy describes the watery, damp feel of a cold

explanation.surface: A large place that nonetheless feels chilly and damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy describes a place with plenty of space, a direct synonym of spacious.

clue.text: Schoolman, as Bartok in a way

parts.note: Bartok's first name was Bela, so someone like him is a Bela
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A scholar compares himself to the composer Bartok in some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here: A BELA then RD for road.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a medieval scholastic philosopher, and schoolman is the term for such a teacher.

clue.text: The skin as treated in the south-east

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Animal hide being tanned somewhere in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Kent is a county in south-east England, so its adjective describes things located there.

clue.text: Lived with model, unchaste in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lewd means unchaste
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Someone lived with a model and became promiscuous once retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns LEWD into DWEL; 'with' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, meaning resided or lived.

clue.text: State of student turning up sack

indicators.note: turning means the short word is flipped around

parts.note: to sack a town is to pillage it

explanation.surface: A student's condition after rolling up a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupillage is the condition of being a pupil, the state of a student, especially a trainee barrister.

clue.text: Remarkably good, a help working with no males included

indicators.note: working means the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: no men means no males

explanation.surface: An excellent assistant who works in an all-female team.
explanation.walkthrough: AHELP and NOMEN are rearranged together; 'with' and 'included' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal, used informally, means extraordinarily good or impressive.

clue.text: Queen collected books and Queen was an actress

indicators.note: collected means gathered in, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: Ellery Queen was the pen name of an American crime-writing duo
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen gathered up some books, and a queen once was on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellery Queen was the pen name of a US crime-writing duo, so 'Queen' stands for its first word; 'was' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen Terry was a leading Victorian stage performer, noted for Shakespeare roles.

clue.text: A race with soldiers, top soldiers and leading lawyer

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
Michel Ney was a Marshal of France under Napoleon
a general is a top-ranking soldier

explanation.surface: A competition involving troops, senior officers and a prominent lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Attorney General is the chief law officer advising a government, its leading legal figure.

clue.text: Chap with a bias — for the Queen?

parts.note: Roy is a man's name, a chap
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Asks whether a prejudiced man supports the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist supports the monarchy, someone who is for the Queen.

clue.text: Point to a gender change — one crosses over

indicators.note: change signals the letters being altered into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Pointing towards a change of gender as crossing over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' attaches E to the anagram RENEGAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts one side for another, someone who crosses over.

clue.text: Mammals (the last shall be first), named like Washington, say

indicators.note: the final letter of the pair is moved to the front

parts.note: a pony is a mammal
a mouse is a mammal

explanation.surface: A biblical saying about animals, and something named after Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: PONYMOUSE with its last letter E moved to the start; Washington State is named after George Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Eponymous describes something bearing a person's name, as Washington State bears its namesake's.

clue.text: Trial by fire, say, or wood

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Choosing between being tried by fire or by wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval trial by fire was a form of judicial ordeal, so it is one example.

clue.text: Continue to preserve an ecclesiastic

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Advice to keep protecting a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral, a type of ecclesiastic.

clue.text: "Pit"- short for a dog

indicators.note: short means the word is cut down at its end

parts.note: a colliery is a coal pit

explanation.surface: A dog's name is an abbreviation of pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a sheepdog breed, so it is a dog.

clue.text: Favour characters eluding order

indicators.note: putting the characters into order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Showing favour to letters that avoid being sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone is to favour or humour them.

clue.text: William Brown's foot?

indicators.note: the possessive 's reads as has, so the two names hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Asks about the foot of a boy called William Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: William Brown is the schoolboy hero of the Just William books, which makes the name look like a literary reference.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot is a unit of metre, and this one is a short syllable followed by a long.

clue.text: Officer's gone off the scent

parts.note: COL is short for colonel, an officer

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer has left the trail, losing the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a perfume, a type of scent.

clue.text: Ancient Roman turncoat

parts.note: an old Roman figure whose name is turncoat read as turn coat, the word coat with its letters turned about

explanation.walkthrough: 'turncoat' splits as 'turn coat': rearrange COAT. Cato was a Roman statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder and Cato the Younger were famous statesmen of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Winds about, missing the German ways

indicators.note: missing tells us the named piece is left out of the longer word

parts.note: meanders ... winds about
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Something twists around while the German is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are methods or ways of doing something.

clue.text: Gain what was lost in 24 with loss of civil rights

parts.note: to attain is to gain
the German article der was removed in the previous clue

explanation.surface: Achieving something with the forfeiture of legal rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainder was the historical forfeiture of property and civil rights after a capital conviction.
